company_description: HP Inc. provides personal computing, printing, 3D printing, hybrid work, gaming, and other related technologies in the United States and internationally. The company operates through three segments: Personal Systems, Printing, and Corporate Investments. The Personal Systems segment offers commercial and consumer desktops and notebooks, workstations, thin clients, retail point-of-sale systems, displays, software, hybrid systems, and endpoint security and services, as well as lifecycle services, including support and deployment, configurations, and extended warranty services. The Printing segment provides consumer and commercial printer hardware, supplies, and solutions, as well as office and home printing solutions; and focuses on graphics, 3D printing, and personalization solutions for the commercial and industrial markets. The Corporate Investments segment is involved in the business incubation and investment projects. It serves small- and medium-sized businesses, public sector, and enterprises. The company was formerly known as Hewlett-Packard Company and changed its name to HP Inc. in October 2015. HP Inc. was founded in 1939 and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California.

risks.title: Declining demand for printing
risks.summary: Demand for printing products is declining due to digitization, hybrid work, and competition from non-OEM supplies, impacting sales and profitability in the Printing segment.
risks.score_rationale: HP explicitly mentions challenges related to declining demand for printing products due to digitization and hybrid work, as well as competition from non-OEM alternatives. This represents a significant risk to the Printing segment.

risks.title: AI adoption risks
risks.summary: Successful adoption and integration of AI into HP products are critical to its Future Ready 2026-2028 strategy. Risks include development challenges, quality issues, and reputational risks.
risks.score_rationale: HP identifies in its strategic risk factors that execution of its strategy depends on the ability to develop, manufacture, and market innovative solutions. As AI is central to its 2026 strategy, execution or adoption failures constitute material risks.

risks.title: Supply chain issues and cost volatility
risks.summary: Supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures, new tariffs since April 2025, and rising component costs (memory, storage) could impact gross margin and operations.
risks.score_rationale: The 10-K report explicitly mentions supply chain challenges, including inflationary pressures on memory and storage costs, imposition of new tariffs since April 2025 not fully offset by pricing actions, and single-source suppliers for certain Printing components.

risks.title: Increased competition and pricing pressure
risks.summary: Intensified competition and pricing pressure in Personal Systems, combined with emerging competitors and new business models, could impact market share and profitability.
risks.score_rationale: HP explicitly mentions a competitive pricing environment, entry of new competitors with alternative technologies, and targeted competitive pressure from existing rivals in Personal Systems. Changes in the competitive landscape threaten market share.

risks.title: Macroeconomic risks and currency volatility
risks.summary: Challenging macroeconomic conditions, including geopolitical tensions, currency volatility, and inflation, significantly affect financial performance, particularly due to high international exposure (65% of revenue).
risks.score_rationale: HP identifies persistent geopolitical tensions, market uncertainty, currency volatility, and inflationary pressures. With 65% of revenue outside the U.S., currency volatility represents a material risk to financial results.

risks.title: Transformation strategy execution risks
risks.summary: Risks of failing to realize expected benefits from the Fiscal 2026 and restructuring plan (2025-2028) could impact the ability to achieve transformation and profitability goals.
risks.score_rationale: HP acknowledges that strategy execution depends on multiple factors including cost optimization, product innovation, IP protection, R&D investments, and business model evolution. The Fiscal 2026 plan introduces new three-year objectives.
